thread:
alex.k: Heads-up — after the 09:07 deploy we’re seeing a p99 jump on production-west for chat endpoints. p95 mostly fine but tail is ~3.2s. Repro across multiple nodes.

maria.t: :eyes: saw it too. Correlates with the runtime churn from the kernel selector tweak (PR #4821) + microbatch default bump in the canary.

shankar: Quick summary from a local profile: kernel-autoselect now prefers `matmul_fuse_v2` for short sequences but falls back to `generic_gemm` intermittently when microbatch boundaries align with KV cache flushes. That fallback path has a lock under high-concurrency.

alex.k: That matches our telemetry — spike aligns with increased KV cache miss rate. kvcache.miss_rate went from ~6% -> 26% on affected pods.

deploy-bot: Deploy started: prod-west/runtime@commit: a3f9b7c (author: jon). Canary finished 09:05, rollout finished 09:07.

eva: Can we quickly toggle the kernel selector flag back to legacy if it's cheap?

maria.t: We rolled out two changes together (kernel selector and default microbatch max from 8->24). My money is on microbatching increasing boundary contention + kvcache metadata pressure.

shankar: Quick experiment idea — reduce microbatch_max to 8 on 1 pod and measure. If tail fixes, it's the microbatch sizing interacting with kernel fallback.

jon: I can cut a hot-revert for the microbatch default flag only. Rolling that now to a small slice.

sre-oncall: I'll raise alert noise policy and pin routing away from the worst nodes. Also kicking a kdump on one of the hurt instances.

jon: Revert flag rolled to 10% of prod-west at 09:20.

alex.k: After 2 minutes on that slice, p99 for the slice dropped from 3200ms -> 1600ms. But global still elevated (we only touched 10%).

maria.t: Okay, queue a full revert for the microbatch default to restore baseline while we debug kernel selector interactions. Can we avoid a full binary rollback?

jon: Full flag revert rolled at 09:28 across prod-west.

deploy-bot: Flag change: runtime.microbatch_default=8 applied to prod-west by jon @ 09:28.

shankar: Profiling after revert (sampled):
```
peak p99 09:30: 780ms
kvcache.miss_rate: 5.1%
kernel fallback events: 12/min -> 3/min
contention wait avg: 18ms -> 6ms
```

alex.k: Nice — p99 back to normalish (~750-900ms). Looks like microbatch sizing was the primary amplifier.

maria.t: Still want a follow-up: the kernel selector still does fallback sometimes — we need to ensure the selector's heuristics consider microbatch boundary alignment and KV cache hotkeys. Add a guard to avoid picking kernels that require fallback when concurrent microbatching is high.

shankar: Agreed. I’ll open a follow-up PR to add a microbatch-aware penalty to the selector score and add a telemetry counter for fallback-retries.

eva: Also can we add a safety config: if kvcache.miss_rate spikes >15% for >2m, auto-reduce microbatch_max and emit an SLO alert? That would prevent future rollouts causing global tail.

jon: Will do for an ops-safe circuit breaker.

maria.t: Next steps: 1) postmortem draft (I'll start), 2) shankar to land selector change + tests, 3) jon to add circuit-breaker flag + playbook, 4) eva to add runbook entry for rapid microbatch rollback.

sre-oncall: No further action required — metrics stayed stable after revert. I'll mark incident as mitigated and set a follow-up bridge for root-cause sync.

alex.k: Thanks all. Lessons: avoid coupling two perf changes in same deploy (kernel + batching). We'll coordinate future change windows and add canary tests that simulate high microbatch concurrency. :white_check_mark:

jon: Quick note — commit id for flag-change: a3f9b7c -> flag only patch. I'll include exact diffs in the postmortem.

maria.t: Postmortem stub created in #incidents. I'll ping for reviewers.

alex.k: Great job triaging. Closing thread after PMs review. :party:
